role: Emits React components and stories; styling delegated to CSS
realises: Emits React components and stories. Styling is delegated wholly to the CSS binding.
note: Declares only what this platform adds to or changes from the CSS binding. A style key absent here is bound exactly as css.json states; this file never restates one. Props are NOT inherited: how a prop becomes a parameter is this platform's own surface, declared in full below.

boolean.realises: a `boolean` member of the component's Props interface
boolean.notes: Declared in the generated types file with its `default` in the Defaults export. In JSX a true value spells as the bare attribute, false as `{false}`. A boolean classified as a browser-managed state concept never reaches the contract.

string.realises: a `string` member of the Props interface, nullable-widened with `null`
string.notes: Widened to admit `null` by the nullability rule: absent `nullable` means nullable for an open-valued kind (ADR-065). `examples` feed stories and composed instances; they never become a contract default.

enum.realises: a named union type, one member per `enum` value
enum.notes: The union is named for the component and prop; values are lowercased by the enumCase contract, and the declared `default` is normalized with them. The scaffold writes the current value as a `data-<prop>` attribute on the component's root, which is the selector surface the CSS binding's propsToSelectors rule states.

number.realises: a `number` member of the Props interface
number.notes: Emitted as a numeric expression — `count={1430}` — wherever a configuration carries it, keyed to the declared type rather than to how the text looks: the same digits against a string prop are content. A closed `enum` of numbers selects like an enum does.

slot.notes: A slot prop never reaches the platform-neutral contract — its type is the one part of a contract that cannot be platform-neutral, so each target spells its own. React spells the designated default slot as `children` and every other slot as a named `React.ReactNode` prop.

image.realises: a nullable `string` URL member of the Props interface
image.notes: An image registry pointer resolves to a served asset URL at emit. A bound prop carrying an authoring-default example (ADR-088) emits the example as the fallback — `p.src ?? "<url>"` — because composed content is static and without it the child falls back to its own default artwork.

object.realises: a named member interface; values as object literals
object.notes: The contract spells the object shape as its own interface (ADR-111). Stories and controls work on the flat view — each member under a dotted arg key (`margin.compact`) — and reassemble the object at the call site. A member binding pointer (`#/props/margin/members/compact`) reads through member access on the host.

emit: the fill as this instance's JSX children — the scaffold reads its designated default slot from `props.children`
cases.why: Whatever kind the fill is: a `$slotContent` reference composes, a literal string becomes JSX text

args.compareTo: a $slotContent reference on a non-default slot

cases.why: An explicit binding is the only shape that can say which of several slots a fill belongs to

otherwise.why: A prop's spelling never nominates a default slot — with no declared `defaultSlot`, every fill is a named prop and a literal string against an undeclared slot is refused

slotsToChildren.notes: The declared `defaultSlot` is the TARGET component's, read from its contract — never inferred from the key's spelling.

emit: nothing — the prop leaves the contract; the CSS binding selects on the browser pseudo-class
cases.why: Hover, focus, active are the browser's to drive; a consumer cannot meaningfully set them

emit: the prop stays a parameter; the scaffold writes the concept's aria attribute when it is set
cases.why: Disabled, selected, invalid are consumer-set facts the DOM should also state

emit: the prop is an ordinary parameter
otherwise.why: A prop no state entry names is not a state

statesToContract.notes: A prop is omitted only when EVERY concept entry naming it says omit. The concept table — selector and contract disposition per concept — is shared between both emitters and the CSS transform, so the three cannot disagree.

text.notes: `span` by default — or the tag a role decides. `content` emits as the text child; a content binding reads the bound prop instead.

glyph.realises: an `aria-hidden` span painted by CSS mask
glyph.notes: React has no glyph component to instantiate, so the exported asset paints as a mask over `currentColor` — visually faithful, but a decorative box rather than an SVG the consumer can reach into.

vector.realises: a styled `div` occupying the vector's box
vector.notes: Path geometry is not in the spec, so nothing can draw it. The declared seam, shared with the Figma binding's render direction.

container.realises: a `div` — or the tag its role decides
container.notes: Carries its element class for the stylesheet and the root carries the variant data attributes. In a phrasing context the default drops to `span` so the emitted HTML stays valid.

slot.realises: the fill render site — `children` for the default slot, the named prop otherwise
slot.notes: The element side of the props surface's slot kind: the element's place in the tree is where the fill renders, and its `contentStyles` style a primitive fill.

instance.realises: the composed component, imported and configured
instance.notes: `instanceOf` becomes an import; `propConfigurations` become its props. A roled instance routes the role's contract props to the instanced component's matching parts (ADR-067 rule 5).

ellipse.notes: Box plus full corner rounding; arc data is not in the spec.

rectangle.notes: The one shape the platform speaks natively.

polygon.realises: a styled `div` — box only, no shape
polygon.notes: Point data is not in the spec; the element's box emits so layout holds, and the shape is declared lost.

star.realises: a styled `div` — box only, no shape

inputs.from: spec document — ordered LayoutNodes: a leaf is an element name, a branch is one name over ordered children
spec document — a variant's layout is a WHOLE structure layered over the default

args.compareTo: the variant configurations that place this element here, state-classified props stripped; entries OR'd, each entry a conjunction

emit: the element, guarded to NOT render here under the configurations where a variant re-parents it
cases.why: A re-parented element renders in the variant's position when it matches and in its default position otherwise — never both

emit: the element wrapped in its render condition
cases.why: An element only some variants place exists in the emitted tree exactly when a placing configuration matches

emit: the element at its tree position, children recursed in authored order — instances and glyphs claimed by their emitters, everything else a container whose tag the semanticsAndTags rule decides
cases.why: The walk is the structure; order is the spec's

otherwise.why: An element absent from every layout renders nowhere

layoutWalk.notes: The tree operations are one shared module, so the two emitters cannot walk differently. CSS has no tree: structure reaches the stylesheet only as root-scoped element selectors.

inputs.from: spec anatomy (ADR-067) — what the element IS, at most one
spec anatomy (ADR-087) — what activating it DOES, any number
declared conventions, through the shared concept table — which prop carries a concept
the emitting tree — whether an ancestor role constrains this element to phrasing content

emit: the role's tag — a `button`, an `a`, an `input` — void tags self-closing
tagCases.why: A role names a control the platform has a native element for
Text is phrasing content, and inside a phrasing ancestor a `div` would be invalid HTML

emit: nothing from the generic path — the role emits the platform-native mechanism: a real `disabled`, a real `checked`
ariaCases.why: Role over states for the mechanism; the states entry still names the driving prop, and the stylesheet still writes the concept's selector

args.compareTo: shared with a concept the role claimed

ariaCases.why: One prop cannot announce two ways at once — a button carrying both `aria-pressed` and `aria-selected` disagrees with itself, and the second is not even valid on that role

emit: the concept's aria attribute, written when the driving prop is set
ariaCases.why: The generic path, from the shared concept table

emit: one composed closure per event: the role's logic, then the role's contract prop, then each action body in annotation order
handlerCases.why: A consumer listening on the prop hears the event before an action can unmount the component
Composing costs nothing when nothing composes

emit: no control of this component's own — the role's contract props route to the instanced component's matching parts (ADR-067 rule 5)
routingCases.why: A role on an instance is a routing signal; the composed component keeps its own control and renders it itself

emit: the default tag, no ARIA, no handlers
otherwise.why: An element with no role, no state entry and no action keeps the pre-roles behavior

semanticsAndTags.notes: The precedence module is shared with the Web Components emitter, so the two platforms resolve collisions identically. Cross-concern by nature: it reads anatomy roles, props classifications and actions to emit one element.

roles.$comment: Role concept dispositions for this platform — implemented (the emitter realises the concept) or inert (recognized vocabulary that currently renders as if unannotated). The implemented set mirrors the emitter's role registry plus the shared part concepts; a registry change must update this block.

decrement.notes: Vocabulary concept only; no docs page worked through and no emitter — the annotation rides inert.

group.notes: Vocabulary concept with a docs page; no emitter yet — the annotation rides inert and the element renders as if unannotated.

increment.notes: Vocabulary concept only; no docs page worked through and no emitter — the annotation rides inert.

password.notes: Vocabulary concept with a docs page; no emitter yet — the annotation rides inert and the element renders as if unannotated.

radio.notes: Vocabulary concept with a docs page; no emitter yet — the annotation rides inert and the element renders as if unannotated.

searchbox.notes: Vocabulary concept with a docs page; no emitter yet — the annotation rides inert and the element renders as if unannotated.

slider.notes: Vocabulary concept only; no docs page worked through and no emitter — the annotation rides inert.

spinbutton.notes: Vocabulary concept only; no docs page worked through and no emitter — the annotation rides inert.

textarea.notes: Vocabulary concept with a docs page; no emitter yet — the annotation rides inert and the element renders as if unannotated.

token.realises: nothing directly — styling is the CSS binding's
token.notes: The emitter never reads a `$token`; tokens reach React only through the stylesheet the CSS binding declares.

binding.realises: prop access on the component — `p.<key>`, member pointers through member access
binding.notes: A `$binding` at a content, instanceOf or configuration site reads the bound prop at render; a member pointer (`#/props/x/members/y`, ADR-111) reads through the object prop. An image-bearing binding emits its authoring-default example as the fallback (ADR-063/088).

slotContent.realises: recursive JSX composition from the registries
slotContent.notes: A `$slotContent` pointer resolves its registry entry and composes it — imports collected, nested fills recursed, provenance commented. Which render site it lands in is the slotsToChildren rule under Props.

subcomponent.realises: an import of the sibling subcomponent's emitted component
subcomponent.notes: `#/subcomponents/<key>` resolves to the emitted sibling and renders as an ordinary composed instance.

elementType.notes: External type references are a consumer concern (ADR-012); the emitter types elements by `ElementType` string only.

image.notes: An `$image` pointer resolves to the registry entry's served URL at emit — in props, configurations, and composed content alike.

nested.notes: The emitter never reads `$nested`: deep configuration reaches emitted examples through the slot-content graph instead — each registry entry carries its own configurations, and composition recurses (DSPEC-05's division of labour).

literal.notes: Style values are the CSS binding's; the emitter never reads them.

mixed.notes: As the CSS binding declares: nothing is emitted for the sentinel.

conditional.notes: As the CSS binding declares: the condition is discarded on the way to a stylesheet.

surfaces.note: The platform-shaped questions this binding owes, none of which are CSS. propsToParameters, slotsToChildren and variantsToSelection graduated into concepts.props and concepts.propRules above; variant selection itself is the CSS binding's propsToSelectors rule.
